title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten officially documented UMKC rituals, symbols and recurring campus traditions that connect Roos across generations.

cards.title: Sing the 2018 fight song
cards.subtitle: A revived song with “Kangarooters” roots
cards.notes: Listen for the fight song at a home athletics event, then join the chorus if you know it. Its 2018 version drew lyrical inspiration from archival “Kangarooters.”
cards.short_summary: A modern UMKC fight song built from an older Kansas City University discovery.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC says its fight song was newly established in 2018 and was inspired by lyrics from an archival Kansas City University song titled “Kangarooters.”
cards.access_notes: UMKC identifies the song as a mainstay at home athletics events.

cards.title: Make the Roo Up sign
cards.subtitle: Kangaroo ears and nose, made by hand
cards.notes: Raise your index and pinky fingers for ears, then bring the other fingers forward for the nose. Use it in photos or while supporting the Roos at an event.
cards.short_summary: UMKC’s 2018 hand gesture turns a hand into a stylized kangaroo face.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC calls Roo Up a tradition adopted in 2018 and specifies how the fingers form the kangaroo’s ears and nose.
cards.access_notes: The university says Roo Up appears across campus and at sporting events.

cards.title: Join the alma mater
cards.subtitle: A song first sung to the Men’s Glee Club in 1940
cards.notes: Learn the refrain before a home sporting event and sing with the crowd. The words celebrate UMKC’s blue and gold and connect today’s Roos with earlier classes.
cards.short_summary: A 1940 school song still sung at UMKC home sporting events.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC states that its alma mater was first sung to the Men’s Glee Club in 1940 and is sung at all UMKC home sporting events.
cards.access_notes: UMKC says the alma mater is sung at all home sporting events.

cards.title: Wear the school colors
cards.subtitle: Student council chose the palette in 1934
cards.notes: Choose Roo blue and gold for a campus event or photo. The color pairing is a student-established part of UMKC identity, reaching back to the university’s early years.
cards.short_summary: UMKC’s official colors have been old gold and royal blue since 1934.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC says the student council named “old gold and royal blue” the official school colors in 1934 and that they remain in use.
cards.access_notes: This is a school-spirit practice suitable for campus and athletics events.

cards.title: Show up Roo Blue on Friday
cards.subtitle: The weekly blue-and-gold spirit cue
cards.notes: Plan a Roo blue item for Friday and wear it around campus or at a Roos event. Keep the look simple: the tradition is the shared color, not a required outfit.
cards.short_summary: A Friday ritual of wearing Roo Blue in support of the KC Roos.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC defines Roo Blue Fridays as Fridays when the campus wears Roo Blue to support the KC Roos.
cards.access_notes: Observed on Fridays; participation is a personal apparel choice.

cards.title: Spot the KC Roo
cards.subtitle: The 1937 kangaroo mascot with a Disney connection
cards.notes: Look for the mascot at a campus gathering or athletics event, and notice the classic Roo imagery too. The Roo story began before UMKC had an athletics department.
cards.short_summary: UMKC’s kangaroo mascot dates to 1937 and its original version was drawn by Walt Disney.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC says Kasey the Kangaroo, now known as the KC Roo, became UKC’s official mascot in 1937 and that Walt Disney drafted the original version.
cards.access_notes: The mascot is associated with campus and sporting-event spirit activity.

cards.title: Mark UMKC’s anniversary week
cards.subtitle: Late October campus-and-city celebration
cards.notes: Check the university calendar during the last week in October and choose an event that fits your schedule. Activities have included arts, athletics, service and alumni programs.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing late-October tradition commemorating UMKC’s anniversary.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC describes Blue and Gold Week as a long-standing tradition during the last week in October that commemorates the university’s anniversary.
cards.access_notes: UMKC says activities take place on both campuses and around Kansas City during the last week in October.

cards.title: Look for the Regalia Run
cards.subtitle: A Blue and Gold Week annual event
cards.notes: Watch Blue and Gold Week announcements for the annual Regalia Run and follow the event’s posted participation details. It is one of the named activities in UMKC’s anniversary-week program.
cards.short_summary: The annual Regalia Run is a named component of UMKC’s Blue and Gold Week.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC lists the annual Regalia Run among the activities held for Blue and Gold Week.
cards.access_notes: Check current Blue and Gold Week event details before participating.

cards.title: Document your Traditions Challenge
cards.subtitle: A photo-based UMKC experience checklist
cards.notes: Enroll through RooGroups, photograph each completed item, and submit your progress there. The challenge is designed to connect participants with campus and Kansas City experiences.
cards.short_summary: UMKC’s challenge asks students to document distinct traditions and experiences.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC instructs participants to sign up in RooGroups, take photos while completing list items and submit those photos to track progress.
cards.access_notes: Registration and photo submission are handled through RooGroups; review current challenge requirements there.

cards.title: Earn Traditions Keeper status
cards.subtitle: A graduation-year celebration for challenge completers
cards.notes: If you complete the Traditions Challenge, follow the listed graduation-semester deadline and contact the program as directed. Eligible graduating students are invited to the annual celebration.
cards.short_summary: Graduating students who finish the challenge can be recognized as Traditions Keepers.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC says graduating students who complete the Traditions Challenge are invited to a celebratory ceremony each year as Traditions Keepers.
cards.access_notes: UMKC lists completion deadlines of March 31 for spring graduation and October 31 for fall graduation.
